checklist.scheduling: File & serve the motion, then email the judicial assistant (not the office phone) with case number, copy of motion, requested date, counsel names and length. Calendar opens 90 days in advance; the requestor must confirm the selected date within 3 business days (else deemed waived) and file a filed/served Notice of Hearing within 5 business days of confirmation. Trials are set via a Rule 1.440 at-issue notice plus email to the assistant. Discovery-dispute hearings are generally allotted up to 30 minutes (longer needs a detailed explanation).
checklist.conferral: Before requesting a hearing, counsel must certify the motion was received by opposing counsel and that the requestor 'conferred with the opposing counsel/party in a good faith effort to resolve the matter without a hearing.' For proposed orders, the cover letter must state opposing counsel agrees or was given at least 7 days to object. Individual 'Form Order Requiring Good Faith Conferral' and 'Bay County Rules Related to Discovery Matters' links exist on the profile but were not fetched (form/discovery-specific); retained as links.
checklist.submissions: Hearing materials should go via a Microsoft OneDrive drop box requested from the assistant; hard copy must be received at least 3 business days before the hearing; 'DO NOT email copies of hearing documents to the judicial assistant.' Evidence and witness lists are exchanged 5 days before; the witness list is emailed to the Court 3 days before.
checklist.proposed_orders: Submit via the 14th Judicial Circuit e-filing portal with a .pdf cover letter. Contested orders are NOT submitted via the e-portal — instead email them to the assistant and schedule a hearing; non-compliant orders will not be entered. The shared circuit proposed-order guide was reviewed at checkpoint 7715 and reused (not re-fetched).
checklist.courtesy_copies: The individual procedures do not use the term 'courtesy copies.' The stated equivalent is the OneDrive drop box submission method with an express prohibition on emailing hearing documents to the assistant ('DO NOT email copies of hearing documents to the judicial assistant.'). The office does not mail signed-order copies; signed orders are served on e-portal-registered counsel, and counsel must serve any non-registered (e.g. pro se) party.
checklist.remote_appearance: All non-evidentiary hearings are by telephone or Zoom until further notice. Evidentiary hearings <=1 hour are by Zoom; >60 minutes are in-person at the Bay County Courthouse. An in-person request for a non-evidentiary hearing must be made in writing with a specific basis. Judge-specific Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/6159006238, Meeting ID 615 900 6238, phone 1-312-626-6799 or 1-646-558-8656. This establishes individual remote permission (not a general Zoom link).
checklist.communications: All email communications to the Court must be copied to all parties/counsel of record and include the clerk's assigned case number in the subject line. Questions go to Mira Phillips at 850-747-5320. Office (850) 747-5320; Fax (850) 747-5159; assistant phillipsm@jud14.flcourts.org.
